correctness.rationale: Bidirectionality identifies stable extensions with maximal independent sets. Such nonempty path sets have first and last selections within one vertex of the ends and successive gaps 2 or 3. Each membership column contributes at most two to the sum of three pair distances, giving the stated upper bound. The six bases satisfy independence and domination; inserting the three singleton columns adds two to every distance. In the order-nine family the first A,BC replacement leaves A,C at the anchor; subsequent steps use the A,C rule with the same inserted block and the unchanged fourth column B. The complete order-six gap list gives the five-cycle at distance at least four; a triple attains three. Orders one to three have counts 1,2,2. Independent gap enumeration and forward-bitset triangle detection reproduce the exact optima for orders 4–20 (python /workspace/independent_checks.py 1); this finite check is separate from the insertion proof.
residual_risks: No claim for directed paths of different orientation, larger packings, or a classification of optimal triples.

value.rationale: Three viewpoints are the first case where a maximally distant pair does not solve the packing problem. Knowing exactly when stability imposes a loss relative to the unrestricted binary bound gives a complete natural benchmark, and the unique exception is analytically explained rather than tabulated.
residual_risks: The result does not give a general diversity algorithm or cover larger numbers of viewpoints.
